Build a Transition Frequency Matrix

Source: R/frequencies.R
frequencies.Rd

frequencies() counts how often each state is followed by each other state across all sequences and returns the counts as a square integer matrix. It reads an event log (one row per event, action set) or a wide table (one row per sequence, one column per position).

Usage

frequencies(
  data,
  action = NULL,
  id = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  cols = NULL,
  format = c("auto", "long", "wide")
)

# S3 method for class 'nest_transition_counts'
summary(object, ...)

Arguments

data

A data frame of sequences: an event log or a wide table.

action

The column holding each event's state; setting it declares an event log. Default NULL. Column names give no role: a column called Action with nothing declared raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input, and so does an action not in data.

id

The column(s) identifying sequences. Default NULL. In an event log, each unique combination of their values is one sequence, and without id all rows form a single sequence. In a wide table, they are left out of the state columns. A column not in data raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input.

time

The column that orders the events of each sequence in an event log. Default NULL: events keep their row order. A wide table does not use it and leaves it out of the positions. A column not in data, or one also listed in cols, raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input.

cols

The state columns of a wide table; setting them declares a wide table. Default NULL. With neither action nor cols, the frame must be one column or hold position columns named as a numbered run (T1, T2, ..., or 1, 2, ...), with nothing beside them but the id (and time) columns; anything else raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input, as does a listed column not in data. A single column is read as one position per row, so it counts no transitions; declare an event log with action.

format

How to read data. "auto" (default) reads an event log when action is set and a wide table otherwise. "long" forces an event log and needs action. "wide" forces a wide table and reads every column outside id and time (or the columns in cols) as a position, without the check on undeclared columns; it ignores action, so that column is counted as a position unless cols leaves it out. "long" ignores cols.

object

For the summary() method: a nest_transition_counts matrix from frequencies().

...

For the summary() method: ignored.

Value

A square integer matrix of transition counts, of class c("nest_transition_counts", "matrix", "array"), where mat[i, j] is the number of times state i was followed by state j; the row and column names are the sorted unique states. It behaves as an ordinary matrix and can be passed directly to tna::tna(). Its summary() returns the same counts as a data frame with one row per non-zero transition and columns from, to and count.

Details

In an event log, the sequences are defined by the id column(s), and the events of each sequence are ordered by time (events sharing a time keep their row order) or, without time, by row order. Each pair of consecutive events is one transition.

In a wide table, each row is a sequence and the state columns are consecutive positions; each pair of adjacent positions is one transition.

In both, a missing state (NA or an empty string) breaks the sequence: no transition is counted into or out of it, and the states on either side are not joined. convert_sequence_format() closes such gaps instead.

See also

convert_sequence_format for converting to other representations (frequency counts, one-hot, edge lists).

Examples

# Wide format
seqs <- data.frame(V1 = c("A","B","A"), V2 = c("B","A","C"), V3 = c("A","C","B"))
freq <- frequencies(seqs, format = "wide")

# Long format
long <- data.frame(
  Actor = rep(1:2, each = 3), Time = rep(1:3, 2),
  Action = c("A","B","C","B","A","C")
)
freq <- frequencies(long, action = "Action", id = "Actor")
